[1/3] Plan project asset inventory and forget-from-project with in-use protection

impact_assessment.why: Imported assets can be added and reloaded but never removed from keystone.json or the registry, so discarded experiments accumulate without an inventory.
impact_assessment.benefits: The editor exposes project_assets, forget_asset removes a manifest entry and registry record only when nothing uses it, keeps the source file for re-import, and the console gets a Forget asset control and path suggestions.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 48 and one action; dependency: project context and AssetRegistry; concurrency: editor lock; state: scene node references, material textures, registry dependencies, in-memory prefab payloads, glTF-derived assets, manifest rollback, external file retention.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Check scene payloads, registered material textures, registry dependencies and in-memory prefab references before writing, reject glTF-derived sources with guidance, save the manifest atomically before unregistering and roll it back on failure, and keep files on disk.

[1/3] Plan editor project build/export with a project-relative target and force control

impact_assessment.why: Project export exists only as a CLI command, so the console can edit and preview a game but cannot produce a runnable build.
impact_assessment.benefits: build_project exports a project-relative build directory through the validated export pipeline, returns BUILD.json summary counts, and the console gets target/force controls and a build readout.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 49 and one action; dependency: export pipeline and project context; concurrency: editor lock; state: non-empty targets, force overwrite, traversal/absolute targets, validation failures, large synchronous builds, build targets inside source trees.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Restrict targets to project-relative paths, default to build, reject root/traversal, catch non-empty targets with force guidance, reuse export validation, store only summary metadata, and add success/force/traversal/no-project tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Editor project build implemented: build_project resolves a project-relative target (default build), runs the validated export pipeline, returns schema/target/BUILD.json/summary only, rejects traversal/absolute/root targets with 400, refuses non-empty targets with force guidance, console target/force controls and files/bytes readout, schema 49; 797 tests green, Ruff clean, node checks clean, determinism hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde, describe schema 49, AIKit 6/6; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-editor-build-v1' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan asset usage reporting across the live scene, registry, prefabs and saved scenes

impact_assessment.why: The editor can forget assets but only checks live scene/registry/prefab references; authors and AI clients cannot ask where an asset is used before removing or replacing it.
impact_assessment.benefits: asset_usages returns structured scene-node, registry, prefab and saved-scene references for an asset id or project path, and forget_asset reuses the report to protect saved content.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 50 and one action; dependency: scene/prefab libraries; concurrency: editor lock; state: malformed library entries, large libraries, unknown ids, project path conversion, scanning cost.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Accept an exact asset id or project-relative path, skip unreadable entries, deduplicate references, expose counts, reuse the report in forget_asset, and add usage/path/saved-scene/forget tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Asset usage reporting implemented: asset_usages accepts exactly one asset id or project path, reports registered/kind, live scene nodes (mesh/material/texture), registry dependencies/textures, in-memory and saved prefabs, saved scenes, project membership, reference count and found; forget_asset now blocks saved scene/prefab references; console Find usages readout, schema 50; 798 tests green, Ruff clean, node checks clean, determinism hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde, describe schema 50, AIKit 6/6; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-asset-usage-v1' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan a registry-backed material texture picker with preview

impact_assessment.why: The material form accepts a free-text texture id, so imported texture assets must be typed manually and there is no visual confirmation of the selected texture.
impact_assessment.benefits: The material panel lists registry textures in a select, preserves the current texture, previews it as a thumbnail, and keeps save_material's texture payload unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI-only, no API/schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: asset-filter interaction, missing/unregistered texture ids, preview absence, re-render selection loss.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use a dedicated texture select that ignores the asset text filter, preserve existing values when present, hide the preview when missing, and add static wiring regressions.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Material texture picker implemented: material panel lists registry texture assets in a select independent of the asset filter, preserves unregistered texture ids as missing options, previews the chosen texture from asset metadata and clears the preview when absent; no API/schema change; 798 tests green, Ruff clean, node checks clean, determinism hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde, describe schema 50, AIKit 6/6; checklists: passed

[1/3] Plan a deterministic parameter-driven animation state machine core

impact_assessment.why: The engine has clip playback and crossfades but no state machine, so games and AI clients must reimplement state, transitions and trigger handling.
impact_assessment.benefits: A validated AnimationStateMachine exposes states, parameter transitions, triggers, crossfade durations, clip events and JSON round trips for deterministic game and AI authoring.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new core module schema 1 and public exports; dependency: animation controller; concurrency: pure synchronous; state: invalid transitions, duplicate names, trigger consumption, loop/speed changes, duplicate clip names, serialization drift.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate state/transition/parameter shapes, evaluate transitions in declaration order, consume triggers on entry, use the existing deterministic controller, and add validation/transition/trigger/serialization/event tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Animation state machine core implemented: AnimationState/AnimationTransition/AnimationStateMachine with parameter operators, triggers, declaration-order transitions, crossfades, loop/speed settings, clip events, schema-1 JSON round trips, reports and public exports; docs/ADR updated; 805 tests green, Ruff clean, node checks clean, determinism hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde, describe schema 50, AIKit 6/6; checklists: passed

[1/3] Plan a file-backed .kstate state machine library with editor save/delete/restore and preview

impact_assessment.why: The deterministic state machine core exists, but authors and AI clients can only use it from code; there is no library, console panel or scene preview.
impact_assessment.benefits: A .kstate library stores state machine documents beside animation clips, and editor actions save, delete, restore and preview machines with parameters, triggers, fixed-step advancement and pose application.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 51 and four actions; dependency: state machine core and animation directory; concurrency: editor lock; state: malformed JSON, missing names, library collisions, trigger consumption, record-free previews, history.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate through AnimationStateMachine.from_dict, use atomic library writes and trash restore, fixed-step previews with a record flag, and add library/action/preview/error regressions.
